acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Crocodilians family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Primeval Crocodile, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Floodplain Sovereign archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Ancient gigantic crocodile with broken dorsal ridge, algae-dark hide, wide scarred skull, and a distinct pale belly fault.
Signature mechanic: Three Flood Channels: the Primeval strikes channel gates in order, raising one hunting route and drying another before its crossing roll.
battlefieldDuty: Open and close three water channels, route lesser Crocodilians into bank attacks, then cross the arena with a colossal roll.
constructionDimensions: Mineral reinforcement follows dorsal scutes, skull roof, claw roots, and tail ridges while flexible hide and belly remain biological.
Mud banks crack, stones roll, and sediment compresses along the lunge or roll path without turning the animal into a statue.
counterplay: Block the lower Crocodilian assigned to that channel, then use the resulting dry bank against the crossing roll. Affinity signal: A pale fault opens at the jaw hinge, planted foreleg, side-scute lock, or exposed belly after commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: Mineral armor that removes the vulnerable belly fault
identityInvariants: Every form retains a low four-legged crocodilian body, long tail, scuted back, belly fault, sensory pits, and a jaw-driven attack silhouette.
Tier escalation uses snout geometry, scute height, neck mobility, tail mass, scars, and waterline behavior rather than equipment or wings.
Eyes, wake direction, jaw angle, foreclaw grooves, tail curve, and exposed belly keep ambush and rotation counterplay readable.
telegraph: Its tail strikes the next channel gate and the corresponding waterline rises before any lower form enters.
